replies.author: @jcbrandon
replies.text:
Until about 2020 or so, I owned 10 undeveloped acres just south of the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, just a few hundred yards across the county line, in Lyon County. My partner and I planned to build our home on that land and probably live there for the rest of our lives.
Because of the development at TRIC and the growth it brought to the greater Reno area, the cost of housing just about doubled. The cost of construction jumped out of sight, and with the lack of contractors interested in building one modest house, it became financially unrealistic for us to build on our property. We sold our land and moved to New Mexico.

comments.text: It is not accurate to say that the federal government owns all that land. It doesn't. That land is public land. It is owned by everyone in America. The Bureau of Land Management, the US Forest Service, and the other agencies that are a part of the federal government manage the land. But they most definitely don't own it. We do. And we, the public, have a say in how it is managed. We exercise that voice by being involved, paying attention to what these agencies are doing, attending public meetings where land management issues are discussed, debated, and decided, and most importantly, by voting.

comments.author: @speedomars
comments.text: Your "facts" are off....BLM land is indeed for sale...and it comes up for auction all over NV regularly.  Vegas would not exist if the BLM did not release and sell its land there ( in the past 8 years 2,400 acres of BLM land has been sold in Vegas), and the same holds true in and around Reno.  Tesla, Google and others are picking NV due to a combination of favorable tax structures, strategic geography, and abundant resources (electricity and local labor).  Nearly half of all the energy made in NV is green (geothermal, solar and wind).

replies.author: @speedomars
replies.text: @captwillard3346 Wrong. Direct BLM land purchases are uncommon around Reno, private parcels adjacent to or backing up to public BLM land (such as listings in areas like Verdi or nearby Lyon and Pershing counties) occasionally hit the open real estate market through private sellers.  The Democrats in the NV legistlature have blocked efforts to get BLM land released in Washoe and Story counties.  In Vegas its the opposite.  Land is regularly released and sold at auction.

replies.author: @GeographyEffect
replies.text: You’re right that BLM sells selected parcels. But taking your figure of 2,400 acres over eight years, that’s about one acre sold for every 20,000 acres BLM manages in Nevada, which gives a sense of how limited those sales are relative to the land on the map. The distinction is scale and readiness: selected parcels come up for auction, but that doesn’t make Nevada’s vast federal acreage readily available for an industrial project.
